request.prompt:
SUBJECT — Doune Castle, a late-fourteenth-century Scottish courtyard castle, built in Minecraft blocks at one and a half blocks to the metre. The same castle as the reference image.

PLAN. The NORTH RANGE holds, from east to west: the GATEHOUSE, the Lord's Tower (27 by 20 blocks, 40 blocks tall, a stepped round tower on its north-east corner; the vaulted gate passage runs through its ground floor from the north front into the courtyard; the lord's hall is on its first floor and the duchess's hall on its second); then the GREAT HALL (a long range 30 blocks long, the hall itself on the first floor over three barrel-vaulted cellars, a steep pitched roof, its high table on a dais at the east end against the gatehouse); then the KITCHEN TOWER at the west end (the vaulted kitchen at hall level, the royal apartments stacked above it, a small stair turret on its courtyard corner). A small servery with two arched serving hatches sits between the hall's west end and the kitchen. South of the north range lies an open cobbled COURTYARD with a round stone well at its centre, and three external stone stairs climb from it: one to the lord's hall door in the gatehouse, one to the great hall's west door, one to the kitchen tower. A crenellated CURTAIN WALL 16 blocks high closes the south and east sides of the courtyard, with open stepped corner rounds, small corbelled bartizans at mid-points, and a continuous wall-walk along its top. The castle stands in a green valley ringed by wooded hills.

SCENE 5, FAR VIEW — THE TOP OF THE GATEHOUSE, CUT OPEN.

A three-quarter aerial view from the north-east, level with the upper gatehouse, as an architectural cutaway: the gatehouse's roof and its upper east wall are removed so its top two floors show. The duchess's hall with its fireplace and the small oratory alcove in its south wall; beside it, inside the stepped round tower, a bedchamber with a curtained bed; below, the top of the lord's hall. Above, the crenellated parapet walk and the gabled garret. The great hall roof and the kitchen tower beyond, and the valley below.
request.style_note: Every image in this series is one place drawn in the same hand: a Minecraft Java Edition build of a real medieval Scottish courtyard castle, shown as a high-quality in-game screenshot with a soft shader — every surface made of visible one-metre cubic blocks with vanilla Minecraft textures (stone bricks, deepslate, cobblestone, spruce and dark oak planks and logs, glass panes, lanterns), crisp block edges, no smooth curves anywhere: round towers are stepped many-sided block shapes. Clear bright daytime, a cloudless blue sky, warm sun from the south-west, soft block shadows. The castle is warm grey-brown sandstone in coursed blocks with lighter dressed stone at corners and window surrounds, dark brown-grey steep gabled roofs, crenellated parapets. Draw exactly ONE view filling the whole frame: never a grid, never panels, never insets, never two views in one image. Draw no text, no labels, no captions, no user interface, no hotbar, no crosshair, no border, and no people unless the prompt asks for them.
